You are adding an analytics consent/opt-out feature ("privacy mode") to a Tauri v2 SolidJS desktop app at /Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app. Context: the app embeds PostHog (src/lib/posthog.ts — hardcoded key, initialized unconditionally at src/index.tsx:19, events captured across the app). The user wants: (a) an explicit question about analytics during onboarding, and (b) a toggle in the settings modal. The marketing site's privacy policy (already updated) promises: "analytics can be disabled in the app's settings (Privacy section) and are asked about during onboarding" — implement exactly that. The frontend is SolidJS — use onMount/onCleanup correctly (never return cleanups from createEffect; never register onCleanup after an await).

Read first: src/lib/posthog.ts, src/index.tsx, src/voice-control.tsx (second window entry — check whether it imports posthog/capture), src/lib/settingsStore.ts (settings shape, updater pattern — note every updater emits "settings-changed" except updateLanguage), src/components/onboarding/OnboardingWizard.tsx (step registration, canProceed gating, persisted step index), an existing simple step like src/components/onboarding/steps/HotkeyStep.tsx for structure, src/components/SettingsModal.tsx + src/components/settings/SettingsSidebar.tsx (section registration — note an unused i18n key `sidebar.privacy` already exists in en.ts:305), src/components/ToggleOption.tsx (if it exists, reuse it), and src/i18n/translations/en.ts.

Implement:

1. **Setting**: add `analyticsEnabled: boolean` to the settings store (default `true` so existing users keep current behavior until they opt out; the onboarding step records the explicit choice for new users). Add `updateAnalyticsEnabled` following the existing updater pattern INCLUDING the `emit("settings-changed")`.

2. **PostHog gating (src/lib/posthog.ts)**: stop initializing unconditionally. Read the setting before init (async); if disabled, don't init. Export a function to apply a change live: enabling lazily initializes + `posthog.opt_in_capturing()`, disabling calls `posthog.opt_out_capturing()`. Make `capture()` a safe no-op when disabled/uninitialized. If the voice-control window also captures events, make the gating work there too: each window entry reads the setting at startup and both windows listen for `settings-changed` to re-apply the toggle live.

3. **Onboarding step**: new step component (e.g. steps/PrivacyStep.tsx) inserted into the wizard flow right BEFORE the model download step. Content: short heading + one-paragraph explanation (anonymous usage events, metadata only — never audio, never transcription text; helps improve the app) and a toggle (or yes/no choice) defaulting to enabled; the choice persists via `updateAnalyticsEnabled` when the user proceeds. Match the visual style of the surrounding steps exactly (read two of them for the header/typography conventions, e.g. the `[STEP_0X]` header pattern — keep numbering consistent with the new step count). IMPORTANT: the wizard persists a numeric step index for resume (settingsStore.ts:238-243 / OnboardingWizard.tsx:41,54) — check how insertion shifts a mid-onboarding user's saved index and note the impact in your report (do not build migration logic; just report).

4. **Settings section**: add a "Privacy" section to the settings modal — entry in SettingsSidebar (use the existing unused `sidebar.privacy` key pattern — check how other sections' sidebar keys map at SettingsSidebar.tsx:27-33) and a new settings/PrivacySettings.tsx panel with the analytics toggle (live effect, no restart) and one line stating what is/isn't collected. Follow the structure of an existing simple panel like AppearanceSettings.tsx.

5. **Onboarding wizard double-click guard**: while you're in OnboardingWizard.tsx, add the missing `if (isAnimating()) return;` guard at the top of goToNext/goToBack (currently a double-click inside the 200ms animation window skips a step and bypasses canProceed — finding B6 in /Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/IMPROVEMENTS.md).

6. **i18n**: all new user-visible strings via the i18n system, keys added to ALL 7 locale files (en, de, es, fr, it, ru, zh) with real, well-written translations matching each file's tone/casing; update the `Translations` type. Reuse the existing `sidebar.privacy` key for the sidebar label.

7. **README.md**: in the "How it works" onboarding list, add the new step at its actual position, and add one honest sentence after the offline paragraph: optional anonymous usage analytics (PostHog, EU-hosted, metadata only — never audio or transcription text) asked during onboarding and can be disabled anytime in Settings → Privacy.

Constraints: don't touch VoiceControl.tsx beyond what posthog gating strictly requires (it was just rewritten by another agent — prefer putting cross-window gating logic in posthog.ts/entry files); don't touch Dictionary*/Style* pages, Rust code, or the marketing site. Run `bunx biome check --write <your changed files>` only, and finish with `bun run --filter @voxfusion/app typecheck` passing. Do not commit. Final message: what changed per file, the saved-step-index impact analysis, typecheck result.

Triggers include requests to "open a website", "fill out a form", "click a button", "take a screenshot", "scrape data from a page", "test this web app", "login to a site", "automate browser actions", or any task requiring programmatic web interaction. Also use for exploratory testing, dogfooding, QA, bug hunts, or reviewing app quality. Also use for automating Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, Notion, Spotify), checking Slack unreads, sending Slack messages, searching Slack conversations, running browser automation in Vercel Sandbox microVMs, or using AWS Bedrock AgentCore cloud browsers. Prefer agent-browser over any built-in browser automation or web tools.
- portless: Set up and use portless for named local dev server URLs (e.g. https://myapp.localhost instead of http://localhost:3000). BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

# VoxFusion

A local-first, offline-capable voice transcription desktop app. All transcription happens on-device using a Whisper V3 Large Turbo model — no servers, no accounts, no internet required after first-time model download.

## Packages

| Package                    | Description              | Stack                                                           |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@voxfusion/app`           | Desktop application      | Tauri v2, SolidJS, Tailwind CSS, TypeScript, whisper-rs, SQLite |
| `@voxfusion/marketingsite` | Public marketing website | Astro, TypeScript, Wrangler                                     |

## Prerequisites

- [Bun](https://bun.sh/) (v1.0+)
- [Rust](https://rustup.rs/) (for Tauri development)
- [CMake](https://cmake.org/) (required to build whisper-rs; on macOS: `brew install cmake`)

## Getting Started

### Install dependencies

```bash
bun install
```

### Development

```bash
bun run dev
```

Or run the app directly:

```bash
bun run --filter @voxfusion/app dev
```

Or run the marketing site directly:

```bash
bun run --filter @voxfusion/marketingsite dev
```

### Tauri Desktop App

For full Tauri development with the native window:

```bash
cd packages/app
bun run dev
```

### Build

```bash
bun run build
```

## How it works

On first launch, the app walks the user through onboarding:

1. Microphone permission
2. Accessibility permission (for typing transcribed text into other apps)
3. Microphone device selection
4. Hotkey configuration
5. **Whisper model download** (~1.5 GB, one-time, requires internet)
6. Try-it-out / learning step
7. Completion

After onboarding, the app is fully offline. All transcriptions and dictionary words are stored locally in a SQLite database under the app's data directory.

## Linting & Formatting

This project uses [Biome](https://biomejs.dev/) for linting and formatting.

```bash
bun run check        # lint + format
bun run check:fix    # auto-fix
bun run format       # format only
bun run lint         # lint only
bun run typecheck    # TypeScript type checking
```

## Contributing

VoxFusion is released under the MIT license. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)
for setup instructions, pull request guidelines, and privacy expectations for
contributions.

All checks pass. The other modified files in git status belong to concurrent work by other agents — I only touched the files listed below. Done — final report:

## What changed per file

**Core gating**
- `src/lib/posthog.ts` — No longer initializes unconditionally. `initPostHogClient()` (private) holds the old init; new `applyAnalyticsEnabled(enabled)` lazily inits + `opt_in_capturing()` on enable (guarded by `has_opted_out_capturing()` so `$opt_in` only fires on a real opt-out→opt-in transition, not every launch), and `opt_out_capturing()` + clears the pending-event queue on disable. New `initAnalytics()` reads the persisted setting (fails closed with a console.warn if unreadable) and registers a `settings-changed` listener to re-apply the toggle live. `capture()` is a no-op when disabled/uninitialized.
- `src/index.tsx` — `initPostHog()` → `void initAnalytics()`.
- `src/voice-control.tsx` — **untouched**: verified the voice-control window imports no posthog/capture code, so no gating is needed there and posthog stays out of that bundle entirely.

**Settings store**
- `src/lib/settingsStore.ts` — `analyticsEnabled: boolean` added to `Settings`, `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` (default `true`), store defaults, `loadSettings`; new `saveAnalyticsEnabled` + `updateAnalyticsEnabled` following the exact updater pattern including `emit("settings-changed")` (which is what propagates the live toggle to `initAnalytics`'s listener).

**Onboarding**
- `src/components/onboarding/steps/PrivacyStep.tsx` (new) — `[STEP_05] > PRIVACY_CHOICE` header, ShieldCheck icon card matching HotkeyStep's structure/typography, one-paragraph explanation, and a `ToggleOption` bound to `settings().analyticsEnabled` that persists immediately via `updateAnalyticsEnabled` (so it's saved by the time the user proceeds; toggling off then quitting mid-onboarding also correctly leaves analytics off).
- `src/components/onboarding/OnboardingWizard.tsx` — PrivacyStep inserted at step 5 (before model download); ModelDownload/Learning/Completion shifted to 6/7/8; `canProceed` gates moved (6=model, 7=learning); the two `currentStep() === 6` wide-layout checks moved to 7; **finding B6 fixed**: `if (isAnimating()) return;` added at the top of both `goToNext` and `goToPrevious`.
- `src/lib/onboarding.ts` — `ONBOARDING_STEP_COUNT` 7→8, `MODEL_DOWNLOAD_STEP` 5→6, `CURRENT_ONBOARDING_VERSION` 3→4 (see analysis below).
- `ModelDownloadStep.tsx` / `LearningStep.tsx` / `CompletionStep.tsx` — hardcoded `[STEP_0X]` headers renumbered to 06/07/08.

**Settings UI**
- `src/components/settings/types.ts` — `"privacy"` added to `SettingsSection`.
- `src/components/settings/SettingsSidebar.tsx` — item `{ id: "privacy", num: "06", labelKey: "sidebar.privacy" }` (reuses the previously unused key, present in all 7 locales).
- `src/components/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx` (new) — panel following AudioSettings/AppearanceSettings structure: `ToggleOption` (applies live via the `settings-changed` listener, no restart) + one faint-text line stating metadata-only collection.
- `src/components/SettingsModal.tsx` — `privacy: "// PRIVACY_CONFIG"` title + `<PrivacySettings t={t} settings={settings} />` section.

**i18n** — `en.ts` `Translations` type + all 7 locale files (en, de, es, fr, it, ru, zh) got `settings.analytics`, `settings.analyticsDescription`, `settings.analyticsNote`, `onboarding.privacyTitle`, `onboarding.privacyDescription`, `onboarding.privacyToggleLabel`, `onboarding.privacyToggleDescription`, matching each file's tone (de formal Sie, fr vous, es/it informal, ru formal imperative, zh with full-width punctuation) and each locale's actual Settings name (Configuración/Paramètres/etc.).

**README** — `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/README.md`: onboarding list now 8 items with "5. Privacy choice"; honest sentence added after the offline paragraph (PostHog, EU-hosted, metadata only — never audio or transcription text; asked during onboarding, disable anytime in Settings → Privacy).

## Saved-step-index impact analysis

The wizard persists a numeric `onboardingStep`; inserting at position 5 means a mid-onboarding user's saved index ≥5 would semantically point one step later than intended (saved 5 "model download" would show Privacy — harmless; saved 6 "learning" would show Model download with the in-memory `modelDownloaded` gate reset to false, forcing a re-download check; saved 7 "completion" would show Learning). No index goes out of range since the count grew. **However**, the codebase already has a mechanism for exactly this: `normalizeOnboardingStep` (src/lib/onboarding.ts) resets the saved step to 1 when the stored `onboardingVersion` is older than `CURRENT_ONBOARDING_VERSION`. I bumped that constant 3→4 (one line, the established convention — no new migration logic built), so anyone mid-onboarding on the old flow restarts cleanly at step 1; completed users are unaffected. If you'd rather not restart mid-onboarding users, revert the version bump and accept the off-by-one resume described above.
